payload.task: self_diffusion of Cu atoms in perfect fcc Cu at 300 K by molecular dynamics (units cm2/s)
payload.reason: Premise check failed: the quantity is not measurable with MD as posed. (1) A PERFECT fcc crystal contains no vacancies or interstitials, so there is no diffusion mechanism available on MD timescales; atoms only vibrate about lattice sites and the MSD plateaus at the thermal vibrational value (order 0.01-0.02 A^2 at 300 K). Any finite D fitted from such a run would be noise/drift (e.g. centre-of-mass drift, thermostat artefacts), not diffusion; the MD answer for a defect-free cell is D = 0 within resolution. (2) Real lattice self-diffusion in Cu is vacancy-mediated with an activation energy of roughly 2 eV (vacancy formation ~1.2-1.3 eV plus migration ~0.7-0.8 eV; order-of-magnitude values, not cited measurements). Arrhenius extrapolation to 300 K with a prefactor of order 0.1-1 cm2/s gives D of order 1e-35 to 1e-34 cm2/s (exp(-2 eV/kT) ~ 1e-34 at 300 K). (3) MD resolution: resolving an MSD increase of ~0.1 A^2 over even 10 ns gives a detection floor D_min ~ 0.1e-16 cm2 / (6 x 1e-8 s) ~ 2e-10 cm2/s, i.e. ~25 orders of magnitude above the physical value. (4) Equilibrium vacancy fraction at 300 K is ~exp(-1.25 eV/kT) ~ 1e-21, so any tractable MD cell (1e3-1e7 atoms) contains zero equilibrium vacancies; inserting one by hand changes the system (no longer perfect) and requires a concentration correction. Hence no simulation was run and no number is reported; reporting e.g. a fitted ~1e-9 cm2/s value would be an artefact. Well-posed alternatives I propose instead: (A) compute vacancy formation energy E_f and migration barrier E_m (NEB) with the same MLIP/EAM, validate them against literature, and estimate D(300 K) = f a^2 nu* exp(-(E_f+E_m)/kT) via transition-state theory (f = 0.781 for fcc), reporting an order-of-magnitude result with uncertainty dominated by the ~0.1 eV error in E_f+E_m (a factor ~50 at 300 K); (B) high-temperature MD (e.g. 1000-1300 K) with an explicit vacancy, rescaled by the equilibrium vacancy concentration, to obtain an Arrhenius fit; (C) self-diffusion of LIQUID Cu just above melting, which MD measures directly in ns runs. For any of these, the independent validation with the same setup would be recovering the measured Cu melting point 1357.77 K (NIST ITS-90 fixed point, from /data/calibration/tier1.json) via a solid-liquid coexistence run.
